author: Sofia Alvarez
title: Robert De Niro: 5 Hidden Film Gems
text:
Beyond the Gangster: Five Underrated Robert De Niro Films Every Cinephile Should See A cinematic titan as the 1970s, Robert De Niro ‘s career extends far beyond his iconic gangster roles. While celebrated for collaborations with Martin Scorsese in films like Mean Streets adn Taxi Driver , and Oscar-winning performances in The Godfather Part II and Raging Bull , De Niro’s filmography reveals a remarkable range and willingness to explore diverse characters and genres. This article highlights five lesser-known films that showcase the depth and audacity of a true acting legend.
Born in 1943 in New York C
Killers of the Flower Moon . Even his appearances in lighter fare like Limitless and The Intern demonstrate a playful self-awareness.
Rediscovering De Niro’s Hidden Gems These five films, often overshadowed by his blockbusters, offer a glimpse into the versatility and artistic curiosity that define De Niro’s enduring legacy.
1. Sleepers (1996) Inspired by a true story, Sleepers is a gripping drama centered around four childhood friends grappling with a traumatic past. De Niro delivers a profoundly human and nuanced performance as a protective priest, offering one of his most understated yet powerful portrayals.The film also features a young Brad Pitt , adding to its appeal. As one observer noted, this film is “a little gem too forgotten,” and well worth revisiting.
2. The Puppet Waltz (1982) Directed by Scorsese, The Puppet Waltz is a visionary and unsettling exploration of an actor’s obsessive pursuit of fame. De Niro embodies a pathetic and chilling character, delivering one of his most disturbing performances. Interestingly,a connection can be drawn between The Puppet Waltz and taxi Driver ,foreshadowing the character of the Joker as portrayed in Todd Phillips’ standalone film. and who stars in that film? De Niro, once again captivating audiences with his unique charisma.
3. Everybody’s Fine (2009) This intimate drama, a remake of an Italian film, follows a widowed father attempting to reconnect with his adult children, played by Kate Beckinsale , Drew Barrymore , and Sam Rockwell .De Niro reveals a touching sensitivity, a departure from his typically hardened roles. “It changes and it’s pleasant!” one critic remarked. Viewers in Europe can catch this film on Arte this evening at 9 p.m.
4. Stardust (2007) Based on Neil Gaiman’s fantastical tale, Stardust sees De niro surprisingly shine as an extravagant and humorous pirate. While the film itself is described as “kitsch,” it’s a “guilty little pleasure” that demonstrates his willingness to embrace self-mockery.
5. Secret Injuries (1993) This family drama features De Niro as a violent stepfather opposite a promising young actor, Leonardo DiCaprio . The film delves into the complexities of toxic relationships, offering a dark and intimate portrayal of familial pain. Notably, it was following this collaboration that De niro reportedly advised Scorsese to cast DiCaprio in Gangs of New York , a decision that launched one of the most iconic partnerships in cinematic history. “So just for that, thank you Bob!”
These films, often overshadowed by De niro’s legendary roles, demonstrate the variety and audacity of his career. They remind us that beyond the gangster persona lies an actor consistently curious, ready to explore new universes – a true legend of cinema.
